2607.09971.title: TopoExplore: Topological Discrimination for Archive-Based Exploration
2607.09971.paper_summary: Archive-based exploration methods such as Go-Explore select which visited state to return to using visitation rarity, and frontier methods return to the boundary of the unknown; neither asks whether the unexplored region behind a boundary is enterable at all. Exploration is not just about finding reward - it is about collecting a structurally complete experience for downstream learning and planning. We introduce TopoExplore, which augments Go-Explore cell selection with a periodic topological pass: enclosed unexplored regions (voids) of the visited-set occupancy grid are detected by flood fill (the H1 classes of its cubical complex), and a decaying selection bonus is placed only on their strict entrances (gap or door cells), so sealed regions are never targeted and entered regions retire. On a controlled 18-environment MiniGrid suite (15 seeds, frozen hyperparameters) TopoExplore attains a 1.52x geometric-mean speedup in median steps-to-first-entry over its exact Go-Explore ablation, versus 1.37x for a frontier baseline; frontier exploration degrades when sealed decoy structure appears (0.83-1.48x on decoy environments vs. 1.65-2.11x for TopoExplore), while TopoExplore holds its largest win on hard multi-interaction doors (10.9x). We report an honest negative on Montezuma's Revenge - without wall knowledge, unreachable occupancy artifacts capture the bonus and performance degrades as it grows, isolating the wall-aware entrance test as the load-bearing component - and a preliminary positive on HM3D scanned buildings, where the speedup over Go-Explore tracks scene difficulty (r=0.69) even as frontier selection dominates blanket coverage. The evidence supports a deliberately scoped claim: topology-aware selection pays off where enclosed structure must be discriminated, and remains competitive at open coverage, where frontier methods are strongest, despite not being tuned for that regime.
2607.09971.paper_summary_zh: 基於檔案的探索方法，如 Go-Explore，使用訪問稀有性來選擇返回的已訪問狀態，而邊界方法則返回未知的邊界；這兩者都沒有詢問邊界後的未探索區域是否可以進入。探索不僅僅是尋找獎勵——它是關於為下游學習和規劃收集結構完整的經驗。我們介紹了 TopoExplore，它通過定期的拓撲通過來增強 Go-Explore 的單元選擇：已訪問集佔用網格中的封閉未探索區域（空洞）通過洪水填充（其立方體複合體的 H1 類）來檢測，並且僅在其嚴格入口（缺口或門單元）上放置衰減選擇獎勵，因此封閉區域從不被針對，而進入的區域則會退役。在一個受控的 18 環境 MiniGrid 套件中（15 個種子，固定超參數），TopoExplore 在首次進入的中位步數上相較於其精確的 Go-Explore 消融實驗達到了 1.52 倍的幾何平均加速，而邊界基準則為 1.37 倍；當出現封閉誘餌結構時，邊界探索會退化（在誘餌環境中為 0.83-1.48 倍，而 TopoExplore 則為 1.65-2.11 倍），而 TopoExplore 在困難的多互動門上獲得了最大的勝利（10.9 倍）。我們在 Montezuma's Revenge 上報告了一個誠實的負面結果——在沒有牆壁知識的情況下，無法到達的佔用工件捕獲了獎勵，並且隨著其增長性能退化，將牆壁感知的入口測試孤立為承載組件——以及在 HM3D 掃描建築物上的初步正面結果，在這裡，相較於 Go-Explore 的加速隨著場景難度變化（r=0.69），即使邊界選擇主導了全覆蓋。證據支持一個故意範疇的主張：當必須區分封閉結構時，拓撲感知選擇是有回報的，並且在開放覆蓋中仍然具有競爭力，儘管未針對該體系進行調整。
2607.09971.author: Jason Carlson et.al.
